plan.chapterName: OpenStax Precalculus 2e, chapter 8: Further Applications of Trigonometry
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single-panel diagram of a right triangle drawn in the complex plane, with the horizontal axis labeled "Real" and the vertical axis labeled "Imaginary," each drawn as a thin double-headed arrow through the origin. A filled black dot sits in the first quadrant and is labeled "x + yi." A straight segment runs from the origin out to that dot and is labeled r; from the dot a vertical segment drops to the horizontal axis and is labeled y, and the horizontal leg from the origin to the foot of that drop is labeled x, closing the triangle with a right angle at the foot. The angle at the origin, between the positive real direction and the segment r, is marked with a small arc and labeled with the Greek letter theta. A heavier curved arc of constant radius sweeps through the labeled dot and carries arrowheads at both ends, one pointing left beyond the imaginary axis and the other pointing down beyond the real axis, tracing a circle centered at the origin. Laying the rectangular pair x and y and the polar pair r and theta on the same picture lets the reader read either description off the other. The drawing fixes r as the modulus, the distance from the origin to the point, and theta as the direction angle, the two quantities that make up the polar form of a complex number.

interactionPlan.concept: A complex number can be represented either by its rectangular coordinates (real x, imaginary y) or its polar coordinates (modulus r, angle θ).
elements: Horizontal axis with arrows at both ends, labeled 'Real'
Vertical axis with arrows at both ends, labeled 'Imaginary'
Point representing the complex number (black dot)
Label 'x + yi' next to the point
Line segment from origin to the point, labeled 'r'
Horizontal line segment along the Real axis from origin to the x-coordinate, labeled 'x'
Vertical line segment from the Real axis to the point, labeled 'y'
Angle arc at the origin from the Real axis to the 'r' segment, labeled 'θ'
Right angle square symbol at the intersection of x and y legs
Curved circular arc of radius r passing through the point, with arrowheads at both ends

interactions.label: Angle (θ)
interactions.teaches: Dragging the angle rotates the point along the circular arc of constant radius r, continuously changing its real (x) and imaginary (y) components.

interactions.label: Modulus (r)
interactions.teaches: Changing the modulus scales the distance from the origin; the point moves radially, scaling x and y proportionally while keeping the angle constant.

interactions.label: Coordinate View
interactions.teaches: Toggling between label sets emphasizes that a single location in the complex plane can be described by either its horizontal/vertical steps or its direct distance/direction.

demo_steps.title: Dual Representation
demo_steps.narration: A complex number x + yi sits in the complex plane. Its position defines a right triangle with the origin.

demo_steps.title: Rectangular Coordinates
demo_steps.narration: In rectangular form, we locate the point by moving horizontally by x (the real part) and vertically by y (the imaginary part).

demo_steps.title: Polar Coordinates
demo_steps.narration: In polar form, we locate the exact same point by turning to an angle θ and traveling a direct distance r (the modulus) from the origin.

demo_steps.title: Changing the Angle
demo_steps.narration: As the angle θ changes, the point travels along a circle of radius r. Watch how the rectangular coordinates x and y must constantly adjust to track this rotation.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The rectangular components (x, y) and polar components (r, θ) form a right triangle, mathematically linking a complex number's algebraic parts to its geometric distance and direction.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Axes are thin lines with double arrowheads; 'Real' and 'Imaginary' labels at the positive ends. The circular arc should be a heavier stroke than the triangle legs, clearly indicating a circle of radius r centered at the origin, extending slightly past the point in both directions with arrowheads. When 'Rectangular' is toggled, hide r, θ, and their respective arcs/lines; when 'Polar' is toggled, hide x, y, their line segments, and the right angle symbol. Ensure the label 'x + yi' follows the point dynamically as sliders move.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for theta: the learner drags the angle from the positive real axis, the point moves around the circular arc while x and y legs update, and the link between direction angle and rectangular coordinates becomes clear.
- Slider for r: the learner changes the modulus, the segment from the origin and the circle radius grow or shrink with the point, and r becomes visible as distance from the origin rather than a separate label.
- Toggle between rectangular and polar labels: the learner switches the displayed annotations from x and y to r and theta, the same point keeps its position while the labels change, and the equivalence between x + yi and polar form is emphasized.

authoredContext:
We review these relationships in the figure.

Triangle plotted in the complex plane (x axis is real, y axis is imaginary). Base is along the x/real axis, height is some y/imaginary value in Q 1, and hypotenuse r extends from origin to that point (x+yi) in Q 1. The angle at the origin is theta. There is an arc going through (x+yi).

We use the term modulus to represent the absolute value of a complex number, or the distance from the origin to the point (x,y). The modulus, then, is the same as r, the radius in polar form. We use θ to indicate the angle of direction (just as with polar coordinates). Substituting, we have
